problem: The table mislabels one column and drops two that CloudSim actually prints. In the standard output of the shipped examples the header is: Cloudlet ID, STATUS, DataCenter ID, VM ID, Time, Start Time, Finish Time. The 'Time' column is the cloudlet's actual CPU time (finish time minus start time), not its finish time, so a student reading the table will take a duration for an absolute time. The table also has no 'Finish Time' column, which contradicts the sentence just above it saying 'the two you need are start and finish'.
fix: List all seven columns with correct meanings: Cloudlet ID (the id you gave the task), STATUS (SUCCESS when it completed), DataCenter ID (which datacenter ran it), VM ID (which VM ran it), Time (execution time in seconds = finish − start), Start Time (when it began, in seconds), Finish Time (when it ended, in seconds). Say the two you need for waiting and turnaround are Start Time and Finish Time.

problem: The demo command puts only the core jar on the classpath (java -cp cloudsim.jar:. org.cloudbus.cloudsim.examples.CloudSimExample1). The example classes are not inside the core CloudSim jar in the released download, so the command fails with a 'class not found' error unless the example code is also on the classpath.
fix: Tell the reader to put the examples code on the classpath too — either the examples jar shipped with the release or the compiled example sources — for example java -cp <core jar>:<examples jar>:. org.cloudbus.cloudsim.examples.CloudSimExample1, and note that the jar file name carries the version number, not just cloudsim.jar. Also mention that Windows uses ';' instead of ':' between classpath entries.
